Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

FINISH AND VERIFY work a previous agent started and did not complete. It was killed just before running its typecheck and lint pass, so the code was never validated or exercised.

## What already exists (read FIRST, do not rewrite from scratch)
`app/admin/sites/` contains `page.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `ui.tsx`, and an `[id]/` detail route.

## Purpose
A registry of published sites with moderation review and takedown. When an abuse report arrives there is currently no workflow at all.

## Context (all READ ONLY)
- `ModerationFinding` schema: `id, projectId, rule, severity (high|medium|low), path, evidence, action ("blocked"|"recorded"), createdAt, reviewedAt, reviewedBy, outcome ("true_positive"|"false_positive")`. **The table is currently EMPTY** — `lib/moderation.ts` still only `console.warn`s sub-blocking findings. Another agent is wiring that write. Build against the table; keep a real empty state.
- What makes a site live: `app/api/projects/[id]/publish/route.ts` and `app/api/site/[slug]/**`.
- `app/admin/users/page.tsx` — query patterns (it solves N+1 with a single `DISTINCT ON` pass) and the visual idiom.
- `getAdminUser()` in `lib/auth.ts`.

## What to do
1. **Read and assess critically.** Finish if sound, fix and report if not. A clean typecheck proves nothing about behaviour.
2. **Verify the takedown path actually works** — setting `publishedAt` to null must stop the slug resolving WITHOUT deleting the user's project or their draft work. Prove it: create your own throwaway project, publish it, confirm `GET /api/site/<slug>` serves it, take it down, confirm 404, confirm the project and its files still exist. **Then delete everything you created. Do NOT unpublish or touch any project you did not create.**
3. **Surface the cache caveat in the UI**: the site route sends `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`, so a cached page can survive up to a minute after takedown. Do not let the UI imply takedown is instant.
4. **Check for N+1** in the registry listing. One query per row is not acceptable; read how `app/admin/users/page.tsx` avoids it.
5. **Review workflow** — setting `reviewedAt`/`reviewedBy`/`outcome` on findings is what eventually makes the false-positive rate measurable, which is the thing currently blocking any MEDIUM rule from being promoted to blocking. Make sure that actually persists.
6. `getAdminUser()` at the top of every page, `notFound()` if null.

## Cautions
- This displays other people's private content. Truncate evidence snippets, never dump generated file contents, no impersonation, no editing someone's site content. Review and takedown only — do NOT add delete.

## Constraints
- YOU MAY ONLY EDIT: `app/admin/sites/**`.
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, other app/admin/** subtrees, app/projects/**, app/dashboard/**, app/settings/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- No new white-on-brand-gradient text (fails contrast; known accepted issue).
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean when you finish.** Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.

## Report back
What state you found it in, what you fixed, exactly what you proved about takedown (including the before/after HTTP status), how you avoided N+1, and confirmation that all your test data is gone.

content.text:
All gates clean and all test data removed. Here's the report.

## What state I found it in

Substantially complete and, on the whole, well-built: `page.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `ui.tsx`, `[id]/page.tsx` and `[id]/takedown/page.tsx` all existed, `getAdminUser()` was already at the top of all three pages plus both server functions, and the takedown logic was correct. It had never been run — `tsc` and `eslint` happened to be clean, but the page had **three live 500s** and two claims that had already gone stale.

## Bugs found and fixed

**1. Reachable 500s from prototype-chain validation.** `isView`/`isSortKey` used `v in VIEWS` / `v in SORTS`. `in` walks the prototype chain, so `?view=toString` and `?sort=constructor` passed guards whose entire job is "is this one of ours", then read a `Function` off the map. Confirmed against a running server before the fix:

| URL | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/admin/sites?view=toString&q=nomatch` | **500** (`undefined.toLowerCase()`) | 200 |
| `/admin/sites?sort=toString` | **500** (Prisma: `orderBy[0]` undefined) | 200 |
| `/admin/sites?sort=constructor` | **500** | 200 |

Same class of hole in `actions.ts` (`TAKEDOWN_REASONS[reason]` — `reason=constructor` was truthy and would have been written into the audit log as the stated justification for a takedown) and in `severityRank`/`RULE_NOTES`. Added `hasKey`/`lookup` helpers in `ui.tsx` using `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`, matching the `isAdminAction` idiom already in `lib/admin-audit.ts`.

**2. "Sites needing review" tile disagreed with its own view.** The tile showed `flaggedIds.length` — every project with an unruled finding, including unpublished, taken-down and deleted ones (`ModerationFinding` has no relation to `Project`, so nothing cascades). The view it links to filters to live sites only. Now one extra `count` intersecting with `publishedAt`.

**3. Stale copy.** The findings table is no longer empty (7 rows landed from the parallel `lib/moderation.ts` work). Two branches asserted unconditionally that nothing ever writes findings. Both are now conditional on an actual count — the detail page takes one whole-table count so an empty list can distinguish "table is empty everywhere" from "this project scanned clean".

## Cache caveat

The caveat existed **only** on the takedown confirmation page. The post-takedown flash said "see the caveat below" and there was no caveat below — the offline notice said flatly "returns 404". Extracted `SITE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` + `CacheCaveat`/`CacheCaveatLine` into `ui.tsx` and rendered them in all four places a takedown is offered, confirmed, or reported as done (registry footer, detail page live box, detail page offline notice, post-takedown flash), replacing the hand-written copy on the confirm page. Wording changed from "returns 404" to "returns 404 **from the origin**".

## What I proved about takedown

Threw away fixture `zz-td-mt3jwmn1` (own admin + owner user, project, 2 published build files, 1 draft build file, 1 source file, 1 build, 1 finding), driven through the real UI in a browser against a dev server. Run against the **final** code:

- `GET /api/site/zz-td-mt3jwmn1` → **200**, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` (confirmed on the wire — this is where the caveat's 60s comes from). `/index.html`, `/assets/app.css`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` all 200; `/nope.html` 404.
- Wrong confirmation slug → redirect to `?error=slug`, notice rendered, **`publishedAt` unchanged, zero audit rows**.
- Real takedown via the form → redirect to `?takedown=done`.
- `GET` the same five paths → **404 "Site not found."** on every one, including the synthesised `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`.
- Project row still exists, keeps its slug and name; **all four `ProjectFile` rows still present** (2 published build, 1 draft build, 1 source); build row intact; owner account intact. Only `publishedAt` went null.
- Audit row written in the same transaction, `targetType: project`, `meta: {slug, ownerId, reason, publishedAt}`.

Tested with the correct `Host: zz-td-mt3jwmn1.kodely.site` header, so the incoming Host check in `app/api/site/**` doesn't invalidate this.

**Review workflow persists:** ruled a finding `false_positive` through the UI → `reviewedAt`/`reviewedBy`/`outcome` all written; re-ruled it `true_positive` → column overwritten *and* both verdicts recoverable from the audit log.

## N+1

None. The registry issues a **fixed ~13 statements regardless of page size**: one audit insert, then five whole-table/id-set reads, then three (count + flagged-live count + `findMany` with a relation `select` for owners), then four grouped rollups keyed by `projectId IN (…)`. Same idiom as `app/admin/users/page.tsx` — grouped/`DISTINCT ON` passes over the page's id set, never a query inside a row loop. The one thing I added (`flaggedLive`) is per-page, not per-row.

## Coordinator's audit-log items — all done

- `actions.ts` now calls `adminActionRow(admin, ADMIN_ACTIONS.siteTakenDown, …)` instead of the hand-built object.
- `site_list.viewed` (meta `{page}` only — deliberately **not** `q`, which is nearly always a slug or a customer email), `site.viewed` on both the detail and takedown pages, `finding.reviewed` (`{findingId, verdict}`) written **inside the same transaction** as the verdict update. All awaited before the reads, per `recordAdminAction`'s contract. Verified live: rows landed with correct action names, target types and meta.

**Two things for whoever owns `lib/admin-audit.ts`** (I couldn't edit it): `site.viewed`, `site_list.viewed` and `finding.reviewed` still carry `emittedBy: null`, so `/admin/audit` will keep listing them as outstanding work — they now have emitters in `app/admin/sites/`. Also note that recording every render of `site.viewed` is volumetrically real: my short browser session generated 144 audit rows.

## Test data

All gone — verified by re-query: 0 projects with my slug, 0 users with my email, 0 audit rows with my actor. Project/user/session/file/build/finding/audit rows all explicitly deleted. Global state back to where I found it (4 live sites, 7 findings, 0 audit rows). The temporary `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-verify` checkout and its dev server are removed; `kodely-prod/node_modules` intact.

**I did not touch anything I didn't create.** Note for you: three pre-existing fixtures — `zz-sites-probe-phish`, `zz-sites-probe-clean`, `zz-sites-probe-wallet`, owned by `zz-sites-probe-owner@example.invalid`, all currently **live** and carrying the 7 findings — were created at 2026-08-21 20:57 by another agent. They're almost certainly the moderation agent's active fixtures, so I left them alone; they'll need cleaning up by whoever owns them.

**Gates:** `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` both clean, zero output. (The one pre-existing warning, unused `db` in `lib/moderation.ts`, has since been resolved by that agent.)
